text:
Winnipeg out-played Chicago for the final 40 minutes and still lost, because Artyom Levshunov found a wrist shot 1:37 into overtime. Connor Bedard and Patrick Kane set it up, a fitting end for a line that had been on the ice for 1.64 expected goals for and 1.07 against. By the full-game numbers the Jets deserved to win 56 percent of the time, with 3.77 expected goals to CHI's 3.41 and 66 shot attempts to 47.

The Blackhawks built their lead early and cheaply. Bedard scored on the power play at 8:11, Frank Nazar made it 2-0 at 15:10, and Ryan Donato made it 3-1 at 17:11, 14 seconds after Neal Pionk's 2 percent slap shot had cut the deficit. CHI out-chanced WPG 1.67 to 0.69 in expected goals in that period, and Bedard also had a 25 percent look that Stuart Skinner stopped.

After that, the game tilted hard. WPG held a 1.44 to 0.90 edge in the second and 1.48 to 0.58 in the third, with Kyle Connor scoring on the power play at 4:44 of the second and Alex Iafallo tipping in the tying goal at 5:39 of the third. Pionk was the driver, logging 25:30 with a goal and two assists. Spencer Knight faced 34 shots and saved 31, which was 0.77 goals better than expected, while Skinner allowed four on 3.41 expected, 0.59 worse.
